# Trame · Rendering

*The graph in force on 30 October 2026, generated by `trame build` from `src/rendering.ts`. This document follows the code: to change it, change the code.*

## Architecture decisions

<a id="MeaningThenLook"></a>

### Kinds and views say what; renderers say how

`MeaningThenLook` · `src/rendering.ts:214` · status: **held**

Kinds and views describe meaning only, in an intermediate format of blocks and inlines (values with their unit, references, statuses, cards, figures); renderers choose the look: Markdown with Mermaid figures, terminal text, HTML.

Context: The same answer is read in a review, in a terminal, in a page and by an agent; a kind written for one format would be wrong in the others.

Consequences: Three points of extension: a kind says what a node is, a view which question is asked, a syntax in which format the answer comes. Renderers compose the syntax elements of their format and never read the graph.

| Rejected | Why |
|---|---|
| Kinds that write Markdown | one format only, and the page would have to parse it back |

- Decided by: trame
- Serves: [A specification that runs](product.md#ExecutableSpecification)
- Applied by: [Rendering of the files](../libs/documents/releases/0.3.0/docs/rendering.md#FileRendering), [Rendering in the terminal](../libs/documents/releases/0.3.0/docs/rendering.md#TerminalRendering), [Rendering in the page](#PageRendering), [Common rendering](../libs/documents/releases/0.3.0/docs/rendering.md#Common), [Rendering does not read the graph](architecture.md#RenderingWithoutGraph)

<a id="RenderedByTheLibrary"></a>

### Trame's documents, rendered by the library of documents

`RenderedByTheLibrary` · `src/rendering.ts:228` · status: **held**

The renderers are libs/documents': Trame chooses their syntaxes for its files and its terminal, and gives the same renderer the syntax of its page, which it still writes.

Context: The renderers were the engine's: the commands of every project need them (build, view, snapshot), and a project's own command could not reach them (decided 26 November).

Consequences: Trame's commands use the library's renderers as they use std's structures; the page's syntax and figures move there with the page.

| Rejected | Why |
|---|---|
| Renderers kept in the engine | a command moved out of the engine would lose what writes its documents |

- Decided by: trame
- Serves: [A technology is changed in one node](product.md#ReplaceableTechnology)
- Applied by: [Rendering in the page](#PageRendering), [Documents in Markdown](#DocumentsInMarkdown), [Figures in Mermaid](#FiguresInMermaid), [The terminal in plain text](#TerminalInText), [Figures in the terminal, as text](#TerminalFiguresAsText), [The page in HTML](#PageInHtml), [The page's figures in SVG](#PageFiguresDrawn)
- Adopts: [One renderer, its syntax a choice](../libs/documents/releases/0.3.0/docs/rendering.md#OneRendererManySyntaxes)

## Technical choices

<a id="DocumentsInMarkdown"></a>

### Documents in Markdown

`DocumentsInMarkdown` · `src/rendering.ts:103` · status: **held**

Trame's documents are written in Markdown: CommonMark, with GFM tables. They read as they are in a terminal or an editor, compare line by line in a review, and forges (GitHub, GitLab) as well as most editors display them formatted. HTML serves only for anchors and collapsible blocks.

In [Local](architecture.md#Local), [Test](architecture.md#Test):

| Port | Answered by | Which is |
|---|---|---|
| [Syntax of the documents written as files](../libs/documents/releases/0.3.0/docs/rendering.md#FileSyntax) | [Markdown writer](../libs/documents/releases/0.3.0/docs/rendering.md#MarkdownSyntax) | a function |

Context: The documents are read in reviews, in editors, on forges, and compared line by line by the advance: their syntax must be text that every one of them displays.

Consequences: Another syntax for the files is a realization of "Syntax of the documents written as files" and this choice changed: the renderer, the views and the kinds do not change; the figures stay a choice of their own.

| Rejected | Why |
|---|---|
| HTML only | unreadable as plain text, and a review no longer compares lines |
| AsciiDoc or reStructuredText | less well displayed by forges and editors |
| Plain text | no links, no tables, no figures |

- Decided by: trame
- Chooses: [Markdown writer](../libs/documents/releases/0.3.0/docs/rendering.md#MarkdownSyntax)
- In: [Local](architecture.md#Local), [Test](architecture.md#Test)
- Follows: [Bridge](../std/releases/0.30.0/docs/patterns.md#Bridge), [Strategy](../std/releases/0.30.0/docs/patterns.md#Strategy)
- Serves: [A technology is changed in one node](product.md#ReplaceableTechnology)
- Applies: [A technology is chosen in one node](principles.md#TechnologyInOneNode), [Trame's documents, rendered by the library of documents](#RenderedByTheLibrary)

<a id="FiguresInMermaid"></a>

### Figures in Mermaid

`FiguresInMermaid` · `src/rendering.ts:123` · status: **held**

A figure (the layers of the graph, the tree of an impact, a timeline) is written in a document as a Mermaid diagram, in a "mermaid" block: GitHub, GitLab and most editors draw it, and it stays text, which a review compares line by line.

In [Local](architecture.md#Local), [Test](architecture.md#Test):

| Port | Answered by | Which is |
|---|---|---|
| [Figures of the documents written as files](../libs/documents/releases/0.3.0/docs/rendering.md#FileFigures) | [Mermaid diagrams](../libs/documents/releases/0.3.0/docs/rendering.md#MermaidDiagrams) | a function |

Context: A figure of a document must be drawn by the forges and editors that display the document, and stay text that a review compares.

Consequences: The Markdown writer puts the lines of a figure in a code block, in the language the drawing says: figures as text in the documents would be the text figures answering "Figures of the documents written as files" too, and this choice changed; the writer does not change.

| Rejected | Why |
|---|---|
| Images (SVG, PNG) | to regenerate at every change, and silent in a text review |
| Graphviz (DOT) | neither GitHub nor GitLab draws it |
| PlantUML | needs a rendering server |

- Decided by: trame
- Chooses: [Mermaid diagrams](../libs/documents/releases/0.3.0/docs/rendering.md#MermaidDiagrams)
- In: [Local](architecture.md#Local), [Test](architecture.md#Test)
- Follows: [Strategy](../std/releases/0.30.0/docs/patterns.md#Strategy)
- Serves: [A technology is changed in one node](product.md#ReplaceableTechnology)
- Applies: [A technology is chosen in one node](principles.md#TechnologyInOneNode), [Trame's documents, rendered by the library of documents](#RenderedByTheLibrary)

<a id="PageFiguresDrawn"></a>

### The page's figures in SVG

`PageFiguresDrawn` · `src/rendering.ts:195` · status: **held**

The engine draws the page's figures in SVG, beside their document: the page shows them as they are, and explores in the browser a graph too large to be read whole.

In [Local](architecture.md#Local), [Test](architecture.md#Test):

| Port | Answered by | Which is |
|---|---|---|
| [Figures of the page](#PageFigures) | [Figures in SVG](#SvgFigures) | a function |

Context: The page's script drew the figures, outside the graph, with its own geometry and its own words; only the exploration of a large graph needs the browser, where it follows the reader's clicks.

Consequences: Graphs, legends and timelines are written by the engine, with the geometry of the decisions of appearance; the place of an explored graph carries its index, and the page's script draws the explorer there.

| Rejected | Why |
|---|---|
| Mermaid in the page | a library of several hundred kilobytes, and diagrams that cannot be explored |
| Everything drawn by the page's script | a renderer outside the graph, whose numbers no decision holds |

- Decided by: trame
- Chooses: [Figures in SVG](#SvgFigures)
- In: [Local](architecture.md#Local), [Test](architecture.md#Test)
- Follows: [Strategy](../std/releases/0.30.0/docs/patterns.md#Strategy)
- Serves: [A technology is changed in one node](product.md#ReplaceableTechnology)
- Applies: [A technology is chosen in one node](principles.md#TechnologyInOneNode), [Trame's documents, rendered by the library of documents](#RenderedByTheLibrary)

<a id="PageInHtml"></a>

### The page in HTML

`PageInHtml` · `src/rendering.ts:176` · status: **held**

The engine writes each document in HTML for the page, with the renderer of every other format: the page has no renderer of its own, and shows what the engine wrote.

In [Local](architecture.md#Local), [Test](architecture.md#Test):

| Port | Answered by | Which is |
|---|---|---|
| [Syntax of the page](#PageSyntax) | [HTML writer](#HtmlSyntax) | a function |

Context: The page wrote its own HTML from the intermediate format, in its script: a second renderer, outside the graph, whose words and layout could drift from the documents'.

Consequences: The payload holds each document in Markdown, in text and in HTML; the page puts the HTML in place and draws the explorer of a large graph. A page in another markup would be another realization of "Syntax of the page".

| Rejected | Why |
|---|---|
| HTML written by the page's script | a renderer outside the graph, with its own words |
| Markdown converted to HTML in the browser | a library in the page, and what Markdown cannot say (statuses, the views of a card) lost |

- Decided by: trame
- Chooses: [HTML writer](#HtmlSyntax)
- In: [Local](architecture.md#Local), [Test](architecture.md#Test)
- Follows: [Bridge](../std/releases/0.30.0/docs/patterns.md#Bridge), [Strategy](../std/releases/0.30.0/docs/patterns.md#Strategy)
- Serves: [A technology is changed in one node](product.md#ReplaceableTechnology)
- Applies: [A technology is chosen in one node](principles.md#TechnologyInOneNode), [Trame's documents, rendered by the library of documents](#RenderedByTheLibrary)

<a id="TerminalInText"></a>

### The terminal in plain text

`TerminalInText` · `src/rendering.ts:142` · status: **held**

What a command prints is text, with the punctuation of documents: indented, aligned in columns, without marks.

In [Local](architecture.md#Local), [Test](architecture.md#Test):

| Port | Answered by | Which is |
|---|---|---|
| [Syntax of the terminal](../libs/documents/releases/0.3.0/docs/rendering.md#TerminalSyntax) | [Plain text writer](../libs/documents/releases/0.3.0/docs/rendering.md#PlainTextSyntax) | a function |

Context: A terminal shows characters: marks of a syntax (asterisks, pipes, tags) would be noise there.

Consequences: A view printed in Markdown is the --format md option, which renders with the files' renderer; a terminal syntax with colours would be another realization of "Syntax of the terminal".

| Rejected | Why |
|---|---|
| Markdown in the terminal | its marks are noise when they are not displayed |
| ANSI colours | lost in logs and pipes, and the scenarios compare text |

- Decided by: trame
- Chooses: [Plain text writer](../libs/documents/releases/0.3.0/docs/rendering.md#PlainTextSyntax)
- In: [Local](architecture.md#Local), [Test](architecture.md#Test)
- Follows: [Bridge](../std/releases/0.30.0/docs/patterns.md#Bridge), [Strategy](../std/releases/0.30.0/docs/patterns.md#Strategy)
